title: Audit Policy Subcategory Weakened
detection_hypothesis: If telemetry is being suppressed at the source, the audit policy change event will record that success or failure auditing was removed from a subcategory.

field_semantics.EventID: Numeric identifier of the Windows event record.
field_semantics.AuditPolicyChanges: Description of the audit subcategory settings that changed.

collection_prerequisites: The relevant advanced audit policy subcategory is enabled for success events.
Domain controller Security logs are forwarded for directory-scoped events.
expected_collection_gaps: Events raised on a domain controller that is not forwarding logs are invisible.
Security log wrapping on busy controllers can drop events before forwarding.
normalization_assumptions: EventID is an integer and Channel is the literal string Security.
Account names are provided without the domain prefix in TargetUserName.
ingestion_differences: Some pipelines rename EventID to event.code or similar.
Directory attribute events may arrive with XML-encoded values.
retention_considerations: Security log volume varies widely; 180 to 365 days is common for identity events.
false_positive_strategy: Benign matches are planned, documented, and target specific noisy subcategories. Tune by listing the subcategories that the baseline project is allowed to reduce.
tuning_guidance: Never exclude the account logon or account management subcategories. Restrict any exclusion to the specific low-value subcategory named in the change record.
test_strategy: Positive cases remove success auditing and failure auditing. Negative cases add auditing, use a different event identifier, and change a policy setting unrelated to auditing.
unmapped_defensive_objects_reason: No Detection Strategy, Analytic, or Data Component identifier for this technique was present in the pinned ATT&CK extraction used by this lab. Defensive arrays are left empty rather than populated with unverified identifiers. Unmapped techniques: T1685.
author: Salvatore Mazzaglia
